headline: Law requires the FAA to create a task force on pilot safety notices and to finish a new notice system with a backup by September 2024.
what_it_does: The law directs the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to set up a task force to study NOTAMs, which are notices that warn pilots about unusual conditions in the airspace system. The task force must review how these notices are published and presented, suggest improvements, and report to Congress. The FAA must also finish a federal NOTAM system and a backup system by September 30, 2024, and brief Congress on plans to make the format consistent for domestic and international flights.

who_it_affects.how: They may receive flight safety notices in a new format meant to make key information easier to find and remember.
The agency must form a task force, build a federal NOTAM system with a backup, and report to Congress by set deadlines.
They will rely on the new federal notice system and its backup for flight planning information.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 3, 2023; the FAA must complete the federal NOTAM system and backup by September 30, 2024.
